title: Carbon's three shapes
caption: Four single bonds put carbon at the centre of a tetrahedron, 109.5°. With a double bond it is trigonal planar, 120°; with a triple bond, linear, 180°. A multiple bond counts as one region of electron density.
alt: Methane tetrahedral at 109.5°, methanal trigonal planar at 120°, and hydrogen cyanide linear at 180°.
description: Methane: four C–H bonds, two in the plane, one wedge and one hash, 109.5°.
Methanal: C=O and two C–H in a plane at 120°.
Hydrogen cyanide: H–C≡N in a straight line, 180°.
